title: Electric Charge & Current
hook: Everything electrical comes down to charge — and an electric current is simply charge on the move.
key_points: Charge comes in two kinds, positive and negative; like charges repel, opposites attract.
An electric current is the flow of charge, usually electrons moving through a wire.
Voltage is the push that drives current; resistance is what opposes it.
Charge is conserved — it's never created or destroyed, only moved around.
content_html: Electricity starts with electric charge, a fundamental property of matter that comes in two kinds: positive and negative. The rule is simple — like charges repel each other, opposite charges attract. Protons carry positive charge and electrons carry negative charge, and most objects are neutral because the two balance out.
extra_html: An electric current is nothing more exotic than charge in motion. In a wire it's electrons drifting along, pushed by a voltage — the electrical "pressure" that drives them. Resistance is whatever opposes that flow, turning some electrical energy into heat. Underlying all of it is conservation of charge: charge is never created or destroyed, only shuffled from place to place, which is why a circuit must form a complete loop for current to flow. HyperPhysics lays out charge, current, voltage, and resistance and how they fit together.

related.title: Electricity & Magnetism Are One Force
related.hook: Move a magnet near a wire and you make electricity; run current through a wire and you make a magnet. They're two faces of the same force.

flashcards.back_html: The flow of electric charge — usually electrons moving through a wire. It is charge in motion, not a new kind of thing.

flashcards.prompt: How do two negative charges interact?

choices.text: They repel — like charges push apart
They attract — like charges pull together

flashcards.explanation_html: Like charges repel and opposite charges attract, so two negatives push each other away.

flashcards.prompt: In a simple circuit, what role does voltage play?

choices.text: It is the push that drives charge through the circuit
It is the opposition to current flow
It is the total amount of charge stored

flashcards.explanation_html: Voltage is the driving push; resistance opposes the flow, and current is the resulting flow of charge.
